# MariaDB Wikipedia datasets

Three datasets from Finnish Wikipedia, for building on MariaDB — vector search and RAG, and
system-versioned tables. Each one can be **downloaded ready-made**, or **built from scratch** with
one Python script from Wikipedia's public sources.

Made for hackathons and courses: the same data for everyone, real Wikipedia ids so every result
links back to the live page, and nothing that needs an account or an API key.

**Download:** every file is ready in this repository's
[releases](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases) —
[S](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/s-2026-10) (156 MB),
[M](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/m-2026-10) (315 MB),
[L](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/l-2026-10) (495 MB), each with
`SHA256SUMS`. The scripts are for building them yourself, or for another topic.

## Which one?

- **Ask questions and get answers with sources (RAG, vector search)** → **S**
- **Show how articles changed over time (system-versioned tables)** → **M**
- **Show that your idea scales to a whole Wikipedia** → **L** (build on S first)

They are not the same data in three sizes — each is made for a different kind of project.

## At a glance

| | **S — History of Finland, now** | **M — History of Finland, every version** | **L — All of Finnish Wikipedia, now** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Articles** | 19,285 fi · 4,921 sv · 5,254 en | 19,742 fi | 568,416 fi |
| **Versions** | the current one | every saved version, 2003 – 1 Oct 2026: **862,076** (12.2 GB of text) | the current one |
| **Text** | clean Markdown (from Wikipedia's rendered pages) | raw wikitext — the only form old versions exist in | clean Markdown |
| **Snapshot** | August 2025 (FineWiki) | 1 October 2026 (Wikimedia dumps) | August 2025 (FineWiki) |
| **Vectors** | **yes** — bge-m3, 1024 dimensions, one per article, all three languages | no | no — a GPU job |
| **Extras** | categories and the category tree | who saved each version, edit summary, text hash (reverts) | — |
| **Download** | 156 MB | 315 MB | 495 MB |
| **Build from scratch** | ~2 h — mostly finding 5,254 articles in all of English Wikipedia (38 GB); +5 h to compute the vectors yourself | ~25 min + downloading 4.5 GB: every version of every Finnish page | ~4 min — two files, taken whole |
| **Good for** | `VECTOR`, vector index, hybrid search, cross-language search | `WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING`, `FOR SYSTEM_TIME`, partitioning by time | scale: full-text search, vector indexes, partitioning |
| **Example on MariaDB** | [mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag) | [mariadb-system-versioning-wikipedia](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-system-versioning-wikipedia) | — |

**Why the biggest builds fastest.** Build time depends on what has to be *read*, not on the size of
the result. L takes FineWiki's two Finnish files whole. S has to find its Swedish and English articles
— scattered across all of Swedish and English Wikipedia — so it reads nearly all of their text, and
Hugging Face's request limits add waits. M has to unpack the edit history of every Finnish page to
pick out ours.

**Two words that are easy to mix up.** *History of Finland* is the **topic** of the articles.
*Every version* is the **edit history** of an article. S has the topic; M has the topic *and* the
edit history; L has every topic, without history.

**Same columns everywhere.** S and L use the same columns, so code written on S runs on L. Every
row keeps Wikipedia's own `page_id` (and `rev_id`), so every result links back:
`https://fi.wikipedia.org/?curid=<page_id>` or, for one version, `?oldid=<rev_id>`.

---

## S — History of Finland, now

*Every Wikipedia article about the history of Finland, in Finnish, Swedish and English, with a
vector per article — ready for vector search.*

**What is in it**

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `articles-fi.parquet`, `-sv`, `-en` | 19,285 · 4,921 · 5,254 | `lang`, `page_id`, `rev_id`, `wikidata_id`, `title`, `url`, `date_modified`, `text` |
| `vectors-bge-m3-fi.parquet`, `-sv`, `-en` | one per article | `lang`, `page_id`, `model`, `truncated`, `embedding` (1024 × float32) |
| `category-links-fi.tsv` | 1,760 | `parent`, `child` — the category tree |
| `article-categories-fi.tsv` | 25,720 | `page_id`, `category` — the Finnish articles' categories |

- **Which articles:** every article in the Finnish category
  [Luokka:Suomen historia](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luokka:Suomen_historia) and three levels of
  subcategories (19,296), plus the main article of each *named* category one level deeper (458):
  famous people and things have a category of their own with their article inside
  (*Luokka:Urho Kekkonen* → *Urho Kekkonen*). Without that step the presidents are missing; walking
  the whole fourth level instead would double the set with lists of politicians and councillors.
  Of the 19,754 listed, 19,285 are in FineWiki; the rest are newer than its snapshot.
- **Swedish and English:** the articles on the same topics — same `wikidata_id`. 2,919 topics exist
  in all three languages.
- **Text:** clean Markdown from [FineWiki](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/finewiki),
  which Hugging Face made from Wikimedia's rendered pages: templates filled in, no wiki markup.
- **Vectors:** one per article, from title + text, with [BAAI/bge-m3](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3)
  run by [Ollama](https://ollama.com/library/bge-m3) — multilingual, so an English question finds
  Finnish text. bge-m3 reads 8,192 tokens; 290 longer articles (1%) were cut (`truncated`).
  **Embed your questions with the same model.** Why this model and why one vector per article:
  the [RAG demo's README](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag#choices-and-why).

**Download ready-made:** the [`s-2026-10` release](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/s-2026-10)
— 156 MB, with `SHA256SUMS`.

**Build it yourself:**

```bash
python dataset_s.py                   # text from FineWiki, plus the ready-made vectors
python dataset_s.py --vectors embed   # compute the vectors yourself (Ollama with bge-m3)
```

1. **The article list** is in [lists/](lists/) — walking the categories again
   (`--refresh-lists`, ~10 min with the Wikipedia API) gives a slightly different list as Wikipedia
   changes.
2. **The text:** FineWiki stores each language as Parquet files (Finnish 1.65 GB, Swedish 3.1 GB,
   English 37.7 GB). DuckDB reads only the columns needed, straight from Hugging Face — never the
   raw wikitext, about two thirds of each file. Measured: Finnish ~4 min, Swedish ~30 min, English
   ~80 min on a 3 MB/s line. Hugging Face limits anonymous requests; the script waits 5 minutes and
   continues when it says "too many requests".
3. **The vectors:** downloaded (119 MB), or `--vectors embed`: ~100 articles a minute on a MacBook
   Air M4, ~5 hours. Ollama needs both `num_ctx` and `num_batch` set to 8192 — with only the first,
   anything over 2,048 tokens is refused or cut.

**Use it with MariaDB:** the [RAG demo](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag)
loads exactly these files (`load.py --vectors`) into a table with a `VECTOR(1024)` column and a
vector index, with search page, evaluation and measured index settings.

---

## M — History of Finland, every version

*Every saved version of every Finnish article in S, with who saved it, when and why — the raw
material for "what did this article say on 3 April 2016?"*

**What is in it**

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `versions-01.parquet` … `versions-16.parquet` | 862,076 versions of 19,742 articles | `page_id`, `title`, `rev_id`, `parent_id`, `timestamp` (UTC), `user`, `anonymous`, `comment`, `minor`, `sha1`, `bytes`, `text` |

- **Which articles:** the Finnish articles of S (the same list). 19,742 of the 19,754 listed are in
  the dumps; the other 12 were deleted or renamed after the list was made. S has fewer (19,285)
  because FineWiki's snapshot is older.
- **Which versions:** all of them, from the first in 2002 to 1 October 2026, oldest first per article.
  One output file per dump file.
- **Text:** raw wikitext. Wikipedia keeps old versions only as wikitext — no clean Markdown exists
  for them.
- **`anonymous`:** 19% of the versions. Saved by an IP address — or, since 2025, by a temporary account named like
  `~2026-33532-4`, when Wikipedia stopped publishing anonymous editors' IP addresses.
- **`sha1`:** the same hash means the same text. A version whose text equals an earlier one, but
  not the one just before it, is a **revert**.
- **Not in it:** versions an administrator has hidden; the dumps carry only what anyone may see.

**Download ready-made:** the [`m-2026-10` release](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/m-2026-10)
— 16 files, 315 MB in all, with `SHA256SUMS`. 12.2 GB of wikitext compress this well because
consecutive versions of an article are nearly identical, and zstd sees them side by side.

**Build it yourself:**

```bash
python dataset_m.py                       # needs 7-Zip's 7zz: brew install 7-zip
python dataset_m.py --dumps ~/wikidumps   # keep the 4.5 GB of dump files elsewhere
```

1. **Download** the 16 `pages-meta-history*.7z` files of the
   [1 October 2026 dump](https://dumps.wikimedia.org/fiwiki/20261001/) — 4.5 GB, every version of
   every page on Finnish Wikipedia. Resumes; checked against Wikimedia's SHA-1 sums. ~35 min at
   1.6 MB/s.
2. **Stream** each file through 7-Zip and keep the listed articles — nothing big is unpacked to
   disk. 1–2.5 minutes per file, ~21 minutes for all 16 on a MacBook Air M4.

**Use it with MariaDB:** the [time machine demo](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-system-versioning-wikipedia)
writes versions like these into a system-versioned table with Wikipedia's real edit times
(`system_versioning_insert_history`), measured and explained — for 50 articles. Its loader reads
the dump files directly; loading these Parquet files instead is the same few lines *(to do there)*.
In a MariaDB table the text takes far more room than in Parquet: the demo's 2 GB of text for 50
articles took 1.2 GB with `COMPRESSED` columns — plan ~5–7 GB for all of M.

---

## L — All of Finnish Wikipedia, now

*Every Finnish Wikipedia article, current text — for showing that an idea scales.*

**What is in it**

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `articles-fi.parquet` | 568,416 | the same as S: `lang`, `page_id`, `rev_id`, `wikidata_id`, `title`, `url`, `date_modified`, `text` |

- **Text:** clean Markdown from FineWiki, August 2025 — the same kind of text as S: 1.4 GB.
  All 19,285 Finnish articles of S are in L, in the same version.
- **No vectors.** At ~100 articles a minute on a laptop, embedding all of it would take days —
  a GPU job, or a sample. Ready-made vectors at this scale exist from
  [Cohere](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CohereLabs/wikipedia-2023-11-embed-multilingual-v3)
  (2.4 million paragraphs of Finnish Wikipedia), but from November 2023, and searching them needs a
  Cohere API key.
- **No categories.** FineWiki has none; Wikipedia's category tables are in the
  [SQL dumps](https://dumps.wikimedia.org/fiwiki/20261001/) (`categorylinks`, `linktarget`, `page`)
  if you need them.

**Download ready-made:** the [`l-2026-10` release](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/tag/l-2026-10)
— one file, 495 MB, with `SHA256SUMS`.

**Build it yourself:**

```bash
python dataset_l.py
```

Reads FineWiki's two Finnish files (1.65 GB) with DuckDB, only the columns needed: ~2 minutes
each on a 3 MB/s line. FineWiki has some articles twice (572,900 rows); the script keeps the newest
version of each.

---

## Before you start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets.git
cd mariadb-wikipedia-datasets
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt       # duckdb, pyarrow, requests
```

| | S | M | L |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python 3.11+ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Free disk | ~0.5 GB | 0.3 GB + 4.5 GB of dumps | ~1 GB |
| Other | Ollama + bge-m3, only for `--vectors embed` | 7-Zip (`7zz`) | — |
| Accounts / API keys | none | none | none |

Every script is safe to stop and run again: finished downloads and finished steps are kept
(`downloads/`, `cache/`, `output/`). Each output folder gets a `README.md` describing its files
and a `SHA256SUMS`, so the folder can be shared as it is.

## Licence and credit

Wikipedia's text is under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/): you may
use and share it, including these files, if you credit Wikipedia and its authors and share what you
make from the text under the same licence. Every row has the article's `url` or `page_id` for the
link. Sources: [FineWiki](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/finewiki) (Hugging Face),
[Wikimedia dumps](https://dumps.wikimedia.org/), the Finnish Wikipedia API. The vectors in S are made
from the text, so they carry the same licence.

The scripts and documentation in this repository are under the [MIT licence](LICENSE): use them
freely, in open or closed projects, keeping the licence text.

## Authors

Robert Silén, [MariaDB Foundation](https://mariadb.org/), October 2026 — built with
[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

"""Dataset S — History of Finland, now, in Finnish, Swedish and English, with vectors.

The ~19,750 Finnish Wikipedia articles on the history of Finland, and the Swedish and English
articles on the same topics: current text (clean Markdown from FineWiki, August 2025), their
categories, and one bge-m3 vector per article.

    python dataset_s.py                    # text from FineWiki + the ready-made vectors
    python dataset_s.py --vectors embed    # compute the vectors yourself (Ollama + bge-m3, ~5 h on an M4)
    python dataset_s.py --vectors none     # text only
    python dataset_s.py --refresh-lists    # walk Wikipedia's categories again instead of using lists/

Safe to stop and run again: finished steps are kept (cache/ and output/s/).

Steps:
  1. The article list. lists/ in this repo holds it: every article in the category
     Luokka:Suomen historia and three levels of subcategories, plus the main article of each named
     category one level deeper (Luokka:Urho Kekkonen -> Urho Kekkonen). --refresh-lists rebuilds it
     with the Wikipedia API (~10 minutes).
  2. The text. FineWiki (Hugging Face) holds Wikipedia per language as Parquet. DuckDB reads only
     the columns we need, straight from Hugging Face: Finnish articles by page_id, Swedish and English
     ones by wikidata_id (same topic, same Wikidata id). Finnish ~5 min, Swedish ~10 min, English
     ~80 min (38 GB to scan) — longer when Hugging Face limits requests; the script then waits.
  3. The vectors: downloaded (119 MB), or computed with bge-m3 in Ollama.
  4. output/s/README.md and output/s/SHA256SUMS.
"""
import argparse, csv, glob, hashlib, json, os, shutil, struct, sys, time
import duckdb, requests
import pyarrow as pa, pyarrow.parquet as pq

OUT, CACHE = "output/s", "cache/s"
FINEWIKI = "HuggingFaceFW/finewiki"
RELEASE = "https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/releases/download/s-2026-10"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/1.0 (https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets)"}
OLLAMA, MODEL, CONTEXT = "http://localhost:11434", "bge-m3", 8192

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--vectors", choices=["download", "embed", "none"], default="download")
parser.add_argument("--refresh-lists", action="store_true")
args = parser.parse_args()
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)

# --- 1. The article list -----------------------------------------------------------------------
API = "https://fi.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update(HEADERS)


def api_all(params, key):
    """Call the Wikipedia API, following 'continue'; politely slow (Wikipedia allows ~200/min)."""
    params = dict(params, format="json", formatversion="2")
    while True:
        time.sleep(0.4)
        r = session.get(API, params=params, timeout=60)
        if r.status_code != 200:
            time.sleep(int(r.headers.get("Retry-After", 10)))
            continue
        data = r.json()
        yield from data["query"][key]
        if "continue" not in data:
            return
        params.update(data["continue"])


if args.refresh_lists or not os.path.exists("lists/s-articles-fi.tsv"):
    name = lambda t: t.removeprefix("Luokka:")
    root, levels = "Luokka:Suomen historia", 3
    categories, articles, links, members, deeper = {root}, {}, set(), set(), {}
    this_level = [root]
    for level in range(levels + 1):
        next_level = []
        for cat in this_level:
            for m in api_all({"action": "query", "list": "categorymembers", "cmtitle": cat,
                              "cmlimit": "500", "cmprop": "ids|title"}, "categorymembers"):
                if m["ns"] == 14 and level < levels:
                    links.add((name(cat), name(m["title"])))
                    if m["title"] not in categories:
                        categories.add(m["title"])
                        next_level.append(m["title"])
                elif m["ns"] == 14:
                    deeper.setdefault(m["title"], cat)
                elif m["ns"] == 0:
                    articles.setdefault(m["pageid"], (m["title"], level))
                    members.add((m["pageid"], name(cat)))
        print(f"level {level}: {len(categories)} categories, {len(articles)} articles", flush=True)
        this_level = next_level
    candidates = [c for c in deeper if c not in categories]       # named categories one level deeper
    for i in range(0, len(candidates), 50):
        for page in api_all({"action": "query", "titles": "|".join(name(c) for c in candidates[i:i + 50])}, "pages"):
            cat = "Luokka:" + page.get("title", "")
            if not page.get("missing") and page["ns"] == 0 and page["pageid"] not in articles and cat in deeper:
                articles[page["pageid"]] = (page["title"], levels + 1)
                links.add((name(deeper[cat]), page["title"]))
                members.add((page["pageid"], page["title"]))
    with open("lists/s-articles-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
        f.write("page_id\ttitle\tlevel\n")
        f.writelines(f"{p}\t{t}\t{l}\n" for p, (t, l) in sorted(articles.items()))
    with open("lists/s-category-links-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
        f.write("parent\tchild\n")
        f.writelines(f"{a}\t{b}\n" for a, b in sorted(links))
    with open("lists/s-article-categories-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
        f.write("page_id\tcategory\n")
        f.writelines(f"{p}\t{c}\n" for p, c in sorted(members))
    shutil.rmtree(CACHE)                                          # a new list needs new text
    os.makedirs(CACHE)
print("1/4 article list:", sum(1 for _ in open("lists/s-articles-fi.tsv")) - 1, "Finnish articles", flush=True)

# --- 2. The text, from FineWiki ----------------------------------------------------------------
db = duckdb.connect()
db.sql("SET enable_progress_bar = false")
COLUMNS = "page_id, version AS rev_id, wikidata_id, title, url, date_modified, text"


def finewiki_files(lang):
    r = requests.get(f"https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{FINEWIKI}/tree/main/data/{lang}wiki", headers=HEADERS)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return sorted(f["path"] for f in r.json() if f["path"].endswith(".parquet"))


for lang in ("fi", "sv", "en"):
    out = f"{OUT}/articles-{lang}.parquet"
    if os.path.exists(out):
        print(f"2/4 {out}: already done", flush=True)
        continue
    wanted = ("page_id IN (SELECT page_id FROM read_csv('lists/s-articles-fi.tsv', delim='\t', header=true))"
              if lang == "fi" else
              f"wikidata_id IN (SELECT wikidata_id FROM '{OUT}/articles-fi.parquet' WHERE wikidata_id IS NOT NULL)")
    parts = []
    for path in finewiki_files(lang):
        part = f"{CACHE}/{lang}-{os.path.basename(path)}"
        parts.append(part)
        while not os.path.exists(part):
            try:
                db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT '{lang}' AS lang, {COLUMNS}
                                 FROM read_parquet('https://huggingface.co/datasets/{FINEWIKI}/resolve/main/{path}')
                                 WHERE {wanted}) TO '{part}.tmp' (FORMAT parquet)""")
                os.rename(part + ".tmp", part)
                print(f"    {lang} {path}: done", flush=True)
            except duckdb.HTTPException as e:                     # Hugging Face: "too many requests"
                if "429" not in str(e):
                    raise
                print("    Hugging Face says 'too many requests'. Waiting 5 minutes ...", flush=True)
                time.sleep(300)
    # FineWiki sometimes has several versions of one article: keep the newest.
    db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT * FROM read_parquet({parts})
                     QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY page_id ORDER BY rev_id DESC) = 1
                     ORDER BY page_id) TO '{out}' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)""")
    print(f"2/4 {out}: {db.sql(f'SELECT count(*) FROM {chr(39)}{out}{chr(39)}').fetchone()[0]} articles", flush=True)
for name in ("s-category-links-fi.tsv", "s-article-categories-fi.tsv"):
    shutil.copy(f"lists/{name}", f"{OUT}/{name.removeprefix('s-')}")

# --- 3. The vectors ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if args.vectors == "download":
    for lang in ("fi", "sv", "en"):
        path = f"{OUT}/vectors-{MODEL}-{lang}.parquet"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            with requests.get(f"{RELEASE}/{os.path.basename(path)}", headers=HEADERS, stream=True, timeout=60) as r:
                r.raise_for_status()
                with open(path + ".part", "wb") as f:
                    for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 20):
                        f.write(chunk)
            os.rename(path + ".part", path)
        print(f"3/4 {path}: downloaded", flush=True)
elif args.vectors == "embed":
    # One vector per article: title + text, up to 8,192 tokens. Ollama needs num_batch as well as
    # num_ctx, or it refuses (or cuts) anything over 2,048 tokens.
    options = {"num_ctx": CONTEXT, "num_batch": CONTEXT}

    def embed(texts, truncate):
        r = requests.post(f"{OLLAMA}/api/embed", timeout=600, json={
            "model": MODEL, "input": texts, "truncate": truncate, "options": options})
        if r.status_code != 200:
            raise ValueError(r.text)
        return r.json()["embeddings"]

    for lang in ("fi", "sv", "en"):
        path = f"{OUT}/vectors-{MODEL}-{lang}.parquet"
        if os.path.exists(path):
            continue
        articles = pq.read_table(f"{OUT}/articles-{lang}.parquet", columns=["page_id", "title", "text"]).to_pylist()
        done = set()
        for part in glob.glob(f"{CACHE}/vectors-{lang}-*.parquet"):
            done |= set(pq.read_table(part, columns=["page_id"]).column(0).to_pylist())
        todo = [a for a in articles if a["page_id"] not in done]
        print(f"3/4 {lang}: {len(done)} embedded, {len(todo)} to go", flush=True)
        for i in range(0, len(todo), 200):                          # save every 200 articles
            rows = []
            for a in todo[i:i + 200]:
                text = f"{a['title']}\n\n{a['text']}"
                try:
                    vector, cut = embed([text], truncate=False)[0], False
                except ValueError:                                  # longer than the model reads
                    vector, cut = embed([text], truncate=True)[0], True
                rows.append({"lang": lang, "page_id": a["page_id"], "model": MODEL, "truncated": cut,
                             "embedding": vector})
            pq.write_table(pa.Table.from_pylist(rows), f"{CACHE}/vectors-{lang}-{time.time_ns()}.parquet")
            print(f"    {lang}: {len(done) + i + len(rows)} / {len(articles)}", flush=True)
        table = pa.concat_tables(pq.read_table(p) for p in sorted(glob.glob(f"{CACHE}/vectors-{lang}-*.parquet")))
        embedding = pa.FixedSizeListArray.from_arrays(
            pa.array([x for v in table.column("embedding").to_pylist() for x in v], pa.float32()), 1024)
        table = table.set_column(table.schema.get_field_index("embedding"), "embedding", embedding)
        pq.write_table(table.sort_by("page_id"), path, compression="zstd")
        print(f"3/4 {path}: {table.num_rows} vectors", flush=True)

# --- 4. Data card and checksums ----------------------------------------------------------------
counts = {lang: pq.ParquetFile(f"{OUT}/articles-{lang}.parquet").metadata.num_rows for lang in ("fi", "sv", "en")}
with open(f"{OUT}/README.md", "w") as f:
    f.write(f"""# Dataset S — History of Finland, now (fi, sv, en)

{sum(counts.values()):,} Wikipedia articles: {counts['fi']:,} Finnish articles on the history of Finland
(category Luokka:Suomen historia, three levels of subcategories, plus the main article of each named
category one level deeper) and the {counts['sv']:,} Swedish and {counts['en']:,} English articles on the
same topics. Built by `dataset_s.py` in https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets.

- articles-<lang>.parquet: lang, page_id, rev_id, wikidata_id (same topic across languages), title,
  url, date_modified, text (clean Markdown, from FineWiki — August 2025 snapshot).
- vectors-bge-m3-<lang>.parquet: lang, page_id, model, truncated, embedding (1024 float32 numbers):
  one vector per article from title + text with BAAI/bge-m3 (Ollama), cut at 8,192 tokens where
  truncated is true. Embed questions with the same model.
- category-links-fi.tsv: parent, child — the category tree. article-categories-fi.tsv: page_id,
  category — the Finnish articles' categories.

Sources: FineWiki (https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/finewiki), the Finnish Wikipedia API.
Licence: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); credit
Wikipedia and link to the article (url column).
""")
with open(f"{OUT}/SHA256SUMS", "w") as f:
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(OUT)):
        if name != "SHA256SUMS" and not name.endswith(".part"):
            h = hashlib.sha256()
            with open(f"{OUT}/{name}", "rb") as data:
                for block in iter(lambda: data.read(1 << 20), b""):
                    h.update(block)
            f.write(f"{h.hexdigest()}  {name}\n")
print(f"4/4 Done: {counts} articles in {OUT}/")

"""Dataset M — History of Finland, every version.

Every saved version of the ~19,750 Finnish Wikipedia articles on the history of Finland (the
Finnish articles of dataset S), from 2002 to 1 October 2026, with the full wikitext of each.

    python dataset_m.py                      # download what is missing, then build output/m/
    python dataset_m.py --dumps ~/wikidumps  # keep the 4.5 GB of dump files somewhere else

Needs 7-Zip's command-line program 7zz (Mac: brew install 7-zip; Linux: the 7zip package).
Safe to stop and run again: finished downloads and finished output files are kept.

Steps:
  1. Download the 16 pages-meta-history .7z files of the 1 October 2026 dump (4.5 GB) from
     dumps.wikimedia.org, resuming where a download stopped, checked against Wikimedia's SHA-1 sums.
  2. Stream each file through 7zz (nothing big is unpacked to disk), keep the listed articles,
     and write their versions to output/m/versions-<n>.parquet — one output file per dump file.
  3. Write output/m/README.md (what is in the files) and output/m/SHA256SUMS.
"""
import argparse, csv, hashlib, os, re, subprocess, sys, time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import pyarrow as pa, pyarrow.parquet as pq
import requests

DUMP = "https://dumps.wikimedia.org/fiwiki/20261001/"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/1.0 (https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets)"}
OUT = "output/m"

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--list", default="lists/s-articles-fi.tsv", help="the articles to keep")
parser.add_argument("--dumps", default="downloads/fiwiki-20261001", help="where the dump files go")
args = parser.parse_args()
os.makedirs(args.dumps, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# --- 1. Download -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
sums = {}
for line in requests.get(DUMP + "fiwiki-20261001-sha1sums.txt", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).text.splitlines():
    checksum, name = line.split()
    if "pages-meta-history" in name and name.endswith(".7z"):
        sums[name] = checksum


def sha1(path):
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


for name in sorted(sums):
    path = os.path.join(args.dumps, name)
    done = os.path.getsize(path) if os.path.exists(path) else 0
    r = requests.get(DUMP + name, headers={**HEADERS, "Range": f"bytes={done}-"}, stream=True, timeout=60)
    if r.status_code != 416:                       # 416: already complete
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(path, "ab" if r.status_code == 206 else "wb") as f:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 20):
                f.write(chunk)
        print(f"downloaded {name}", flush=True)
    r.close()
    if sha1(path) != sums[name]:
        sys.exit(f"Checksum does not match for {path}. Delete it and run again.")
print(f"{len(sums)} dump files present and checked", flush=True)

# --- 2. Extract the versions of our articles ---------------------------------------------------
wanted = {int(r["page_id"]) for r in csv.DictReader(open(args.list), delimiter="\t")}
ANONYMOUS = re.compile(r"^~\d{4}-")      # since 2025 anonymous editors get temporary accounts like ~2026-33532-4
SCHEMA = pa.schema([
    ("page_id", pa.uint32()), ("title", pa.string()), ("rev_id", pa.uint32()), ("parent_id", pa.uint32()),
    ("timestamp", pa.timestamp("s", tz="UTC")), ("user", pa.string()), ("anonymous", pa.bool_()),
    ("comment", pa.string()), ("minor", pa.bool_()), ("sha1", pa.string()), ("bytes", pa.uint32()),
    ("text", pa.string()),
])


def tag(element):
    return element.tag.rsplit("}", 1)[-1]


def extract(dump_path, out_path):
    """Stream one dump file and write the versions of the wanted articles, one article at a time."""
    tmp = out_path + ".part"
    writer = pq.ParquetWriter(tmp, SCHEMA, compression="zstd", compression_level=9)
    stream = subprocess.Popen(["7zz", "x", "-so", dump_path], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    page_id, title, keep, rows = None, None, False, []
    articles = versions = 0
    for _, el in ET.iterparse(stream.stdout, events=("end",)):
        name = tag(el)
        if name == "title" and page_id is None:
            title = el.text
        elif name == "id" and page_id is None:
            page_id = int(el.text)                # the page's own id comes before its revisions
            keep = page_id in wanted
        elif name == "revision":
            if keep:
                f = {tag(c): c for c in el}
                who = {tag(c): c.text for c in f["contributor"]} if "contributor" in f else {}
                user = who.get("username") or who.get("ip")
                rows.append({
                    "page_id": page_id, "title": title, "rev_id": int(f["id"].text),
                    "parent_id": int(f["parentid"].text) if "parentid" in f else None,
                    "timestamp": datetime.strptime(f["timestamp"].text, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc),
                    "user": user, "anonymous": "ip" in who or bool(user and ANONYMOUS.match(user)),
                    "comment": f["comment"].text if "comment" in f else None, "minor": "minor" in f,
                    "sha1": f["sha1"].text if "sha1" in f else None,
                    "bytes": int(f["text"].get("bytes", 0)) if "text" in f else 0,
                    "text": (f["text"].text or "") if "text" in f else ""})
            el.clear()
        elif name == "page":
            if rows:
                rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["timestamp"], r["rev_id"]))
                writer.write_table(pa.Table.from_pylist(rows, SCHEMA), row_group_size=2000)
                articles += 1
                versions += len(rows)
            page_id, title, keep, rows = None, None, False, []
            el.clear()
    stream.wait()
    writer.close()
    os.rename(tmp, out_path)
    return articles, versions


for n, name in enumerate(sorted(sums, key=lambda s: int(re.search(r"-p(\d+)p", s).group(1))), 1):
    out_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"versions-{n:02d}.parquet")
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        print(f"{out_path}: already done", flush=True)
        continue
    start = time.time()
    a, v = extract(os.path.join(args.dumps, name), out_path)
    print(f"{out_path}: {a} articles, {v:,} versions, {os.path.getsize(out_path) / 1e6:,.0f} MB, "
          f"{time.time() - start:.0f} s  (from {name})", flush=True)

# --- 3. Data card and checksums ----------------------------------------------------------------
files = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(OUT) if f.endswith(".parquet"))
meta = [pq.ParquetFile(os.path.join(OUT, f)).metadata for f in files]
total_versions = sum(m.num_rows for m in meta)
ids = pa.concat_tables(pq.read_table(os.path.join(OUT, f), columns=["page_id", "bytes"]) for f in files)
total_articles = len(set(ids.column("page_id").to_pylist()))
text_gb = sum(ids.column("bytes").to_pylist()) / 1e9
total_mb = sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(OUT, f)) for f in files) / 1e6
with open(os.path.join(OUT, "README.md"), "w") as f:
    f.write(f"""# Dataset M — History of Finland, every version

Every saved version of the Finnish Wikipedia articles on the history of Finland, from the
`pages-meta-history` dump of 1 October 2026: {total_versions:,} versions of {total_articles:,} articles,
{text_gb:,.1f} GB of wikitext in {len(files)} Parquet files of {total_mb:,.0f} MB in all (zstd: consecutive
versions of an article are nearly identical, so they compress very well). Built by `dataset_m.py` in https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets.

One row per version, oldest first within each article. Columns: page_id, title (as it was then),
rev_id, parent_id, timestamp (UTC, when the version was saved), user (name, IP address or
temporary account), anonymous (IP address or temporary account), comment (edit summary), minor,
sha1 (same hash = same text), bytes, text (wikitext).

Source: Wikimedia dumps, https://dumps.wikimedia.org/fiwiki/20261001/
Licence: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
Credit Wikipedia and its authors; each version's authors are listed on
https://fi.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=<page_id>&action=history
""")
with open(os.path.join(OUT, "SHA256SUMS"), "w") as f:
    for name in files + ["README.md"]:
        h = hashlib.sha256()
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, name), "rb") as data:
            for block in iter(lambda: data.read(1 << 20), b""):
                h.update(block)
        f.write(f"{h.hexdigest()}  {name}\n")
print(f"Done: {total_versions:,} versions, {total_mb:,.0f} MB in {OUT}/")

"""Dataset L — All of Finnish Wikipedia, now.

Every article on Finnish Wikipedia (~573,000): current text as clean Markdown, from FineWiki
(August 2025 snapshot). No vectors: embedding all of it is a GPU job (see the README).

    python dataset_l.py

Safe to stop and run again: finished steps are kept (cache/ and output/l/).

Steps:
  1. FineWiki (Hugging Face) holds Finnish Wikipedia as 2 Parquet files (1.65 GB). DuckDB reads
     only the columns we need, straight from Hugging Face — the raw wikitext, about two thirds of
     each file, is never downloaded. ~5 minutes; longer if Hugging Face limits requests.
  2. FineWiki sometimes has several versions of one article: keep the newest.
  3. output/l/README.md and output/l/SHA256SUMS.
"""
import hashlib, os, time
import duckdb, requests

OUT, CACHE = "output/l", "cache/l"
FINEWIKI = "HuggingFaceFW/finewiki"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "mariadb-wikipedia-datasets/1.0 (https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets)"}
COLUMNS = "'fi' AS lang, page_id, version AS rev_id, wikidata_id, title, url, date_modified, text"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)

db = duckdb.connect()
db.sql("SET enable_progress_bar = false")
r = requests.get(f"https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{FINEWIKI}/tree/main/data/fiwiki", headers=HEADERS)
r.raise_for_status()
parts = []
for path in sorted(f["path"] for f in r.json() if f["path"].endswith(".parquet")):
    part = f"{CACHE}/fi-{os.path.basename(path)}"
    parts.append(part)
    while not os.path.exists(part):
        try:
            start = time.time()
            db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT {COLUMNS} FROM read_parquet('https://huggingface.co/datasets/{FINEWIKI}/resolve/main/{path}'))
                       TO '{part}.tmp' (FORMAT parquet)""")
            os.rename(part + ".tmp", part)
            print(f"1/3 {path}: {time.time() - start:.0f} s", flush=True)
        except duckdb.HTTPException as e:                           # Hugging Face: "too many requests"
            if "429" not in str(e):
                raise
            print("    Hugging Face says 'too many requests'. Waiting 5 minutes ...", flush=True)
            time.sleep(300)

out = f"{OUT}/articles-fi.parquet"
db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT * FROM read_parquet({parts})
                 QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY page_id ORDER BY rev_id DESC) = 1
                 ORDER BY page_id) TO '{out}' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)""")
n, mb = db.sql(f"SELECT count(*), sum(length(text)) / 1e6 FROM '{out}'").fetchone()
print(f"2/3 {out}: {n:,} articles, {mb:,.0f} MB of text, {os.path.getsize(out) / 1e6:,.0f} MB file", flush=True)

with open(f"{OUT}/README.md", "w") as f:
    f.write(f"""# Dataset L — All of Finnish Wikipedia, now

{n:,} Finnish Wikipedia articles, the current text of each as clean Markdown (FineWiki, August 2025
snapshot): {mb:,.0f} MB of text. Built by `dataset_l.py` in https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-wikipedia-datasets.

articles-fi.parquet: lang, page_id, rev_id, wikidata_id, title, url, date_modified, text — the
same columns as dataset S, so code written for S runs on L.

Source: FineWiki (https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/finewiki), made from Wikimedia's
HTML dumps. Licence: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/);
credit Wikipedia and link to the article (url column).
""")
with open(f"{OUT}/SHA256SUMS", "w") as f:
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(OUT)):
        if name != "SHA256SUMS":
            h = hashlib.sha256()
            with open(f"{OUT}/{name}", "rb") as data:
                for block in iter(lambda: data.read(1 << 20), b""):
                    h.update(block)
            f.write(f"{h.hexdigest()}  {name}\n")
print(f"3/3 Done: {OUT}/")
